items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Louis Armstrong played in his place. And I played in the drummer's place.

ctx.x: But you began working about nineteen sixteen when you were sixteen, you say? That's my first job. I played with a teacher.

That's right, Columbia Band. Mm-hmm. And then after I left the Columbia Band, King Oliver got with Ori, see, just before Storyville closed, you see. And they were working at Pete Lyle's. You heard of Pete Lyle's? Yeah. Well, they were working there. Well, on Sunday night, Saturday and Sundays, King Oliver would go to play with Ori, see, and he would take his drummer. Let me see who was playing at Pete Lyle's then. I can't remember what drummer was playing at Pete Lyle's. But anyhow, Louis Armstrong played in his…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: You said you played with him at Lollars? Yeah. And you played a lot of little parties with him?

ctx.x: And Sam was going on the road every weekend, see, going to Biloxi, Paris Christiane, Bay St. Louis. Well, Manny Gabriel couldn't get off, you see, to go on the road with Sam and play. He was a slate or carpet or something. We was playing at the economy hall one night, and he'd come and ask Buddy to let me go make a trip with him, you see. Buddy didn't like the idea, you know. He figured Sam wanted to take me anyway, you see. I just said come back from California, you see. Mm-hmm. So he said, well, I don't like…

So you were with Buddy a real short length of time. Short length of time, yeah. I wouldn't say it was about too long. Oh, what about Armstrong? You said you played with him at Lollars? Yeah. And you played a lot of little parties with him?

A little, very few. I didn't play many. See, because I left, you see. I must play about one or two, because I left, you see. After we played Pete Lollars, after that 1916, you know, rave. Well, we went in Pete Lollars, you see, about 17 and the war started, come out, you know, broke out. Mm-hmm. And, uh, well, I didn't play, but he went on the boat, I think, or Tom Anderson's one of the two. I just remember now, see. Mm-hmm. Well, he broke up to the band he had, you see.
